tools.name: orderdesk_get_store
tools.description: The store's name, id, FOLDERS (id -> name; orders live in exactly one folder, and folder ids are needed to filter and move orders) and key settings (timezone, locale, stock behavior, shipping methods). The API key and mail credentials are never returned. GET /store.

tools.name: orderdesk_list_orders
tools.description: Search orders, newest first, with items, addresses, totals, payment and shipments. Filters combine with AND. Prefer a date range: Order Desk asks clients to avoid open-ended queries. Page with limit and offset (next_offset). GET /orders.

tools.name: orderdesk_get_order
tools.description: One order by Order Desk's internal id: addresses, items, totals, payment, notes, discounts, checkout data and shipments. To find an order by your own id, use orderdesk_list_orders with source_id. GET /orders/{order_id}.

tools.name: orderdesk_list_order_items
tools.description: The line items of one order (name, SKU, price, quantity, weight, delivery type, variations). GET /orders/{order_id}/order-items.

tools.name: orderdesk_list_order_shipments
tools.description: The shipments recorded against an order: carrier, tracking number and URL, method, weight, cost, dates. GET /orders/{order_id}/shipments.

tools.name: orderdesk_create_order
tools.description: WRITE: add a new order to the store. Needs at least one item, and a name or company in the shipping or customer address (if only one address is given the other is copied from it). Omit folder_id to land in the first folder. Order Desk rejects an order it recognizes as a duplicate and names the exist

tools.name: orderdesk_update_order
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing order. Order Desk's PUT replaces the whole record, so this reads the order, applies only the fields you pass (shipping/customer address fields and checkout_data/order_metadata keys are merged into what is there, other values replaced) and sends the complete record

tools.name: orderdesk_add_order_item
tools.description: WRITE: add one line item to an existing order; Order Desk recalculates the totals. POST /orders/{order_id}/order-items.

tools.name: orderdesk_add_order_note
tools.description: WRITE: append an entry to an order's history. History is append-only (entries cannot be edited or removed) and an order holds at most 250 entries, so do not use it for routine polling. POST /orders/{order_id}/order-history.

tools.name: orderdesk_add_shipment
tools.description: WRITE: record a shipment (carrier and tracking number) against an order. One shipment per parcel; several shipments represent a partial fulfillment. Use "n/a" when there is no tracking number. If tracking_url is omitted Order Desk derives it. POST /orders/{order_id}/shipments.

tools.name: orderdesk_move_orders
tools.description: WRITE: move one or more orders to another folder. Moving runs the rules attached to the destination folder (which can send e-mail, call fulfillment services, etc.) and writes a history entry. Pass exactly one of destination_folder_id or destination_folder_name (see orderdesk_get_store). Returns each

tools.name: orderdesk_list_inventory_items
tools.description: Search the store's inventory (SKU, name, price, cost, weight, stock, location). Order Desk returns every match with no paging, so narrow with search/code/name; limit and offset slice the result here. GET /inventory-items.

tools.name: orderdesk_get_inventory_item
tools.description: One inventory item by Order Desk's internal id. GET /inventory-items/{inventory_item_id}.

tools.name: orderdesk_create_inventory_item
tools.description: WRITE: add an inventory item. The code (SKU) must match the code your orders arrive with. POST /inventory-items.

tools.name: orderdesk_update_inventory_item
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an inventory item, for example its stock count. Order Desk's PUT replaces the whole record, so this reads the item, applies only the fields you pass (metadata and variation keys are merged) and sends the complete record back. PUT /inventory-items/{inventory_item_id}.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "orderdesk_get_store" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "orderdesk_list_inventory_items" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: search, code, name, manufacturer_sku, location, updated_from, limit, offset

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: orderdesk_list_order_shipments · Private data: orderdesk_get_store, orderdesk_update_order, orderdesk_add_shipment, orderdesk_update_inventory_item · Public sink: orderdesk_create_order, orderdesk_add_order_item, orderdesk_add_order_note, orderdesk_add_shipment, orderdesk_move_orders, orderdesk_create_inventory_item.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: orderdesk_list_order_shipments · Private data: orderdesk_get_store, orderdesk_update_order, orderdesk_add_shipment, orderdesk_update_inventory_item · Public sink: orderdesk_create_order, orderdesk_add_order_item, orderdesk_add_order_note, orderdesk_add_shipment, orderdesk_move_orders, orderdesk_create_inventory_item

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
